content_of_post_to_answer: To give tension another one we feel very bad, but why does that tension come to our mind?
answer: Tension often appears because the mind is trying to protect us from uncertainty. It creates possible problems before they happen, not because those problems are real, but because preparation feels safer than surprise. The difficult part is learning to separate useful awareness from endless mental rehearsal. I've written more about this pattern on my profile for anyone who wants to explore it further. A worried mind is not always predicting danger; sometimes it is simply asking for certainty that life cannot provide.
